messages.subject: inla lgcp population intensity
parts:
Dear all, 

I am playing with some code Gilles Guillot posted some time ago based on the chapter 8 of the INLA SPDE manual.

http://www2.imm.dtu.dk/~gigu/share/LGCP_INLA_GG.R

My question is, lets say that we have a population intensity approximated with kernel (based on density.ppp function, im class) how can we incorporate this object in the inla command to adjust for pop intensity. 

Best, 
Akis

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla lgcp population intensity
parts:
On 23/02/2017 05:42, Konstantinoudis Akis wrote:
> My question is, lets say that we have a population intensity
> approximated with kernel (based on density.ppp function, im class) how
> can we incorporate this object in the inla command to adjust for pop
> intensity.

You have to multiply it with the integration weights and supply as
exposure. I'm working in a new version of the tutorial that improves
such example.
Elias

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla lgcp population intensity
parts:
For individual non-spatial covariates, or "marks" (such as age and sex) it depends a bit on the detail of the model you want to build.  We've been working on a package that handles things such as group size dependent detection probabilities in wildlife surveys, where the structure of the combined model for group locations and group sizes doesn't fall under the basic inla framework, but can be handled with some extra iterative steps.  Other types of marks are more straightforward.
The preliminary package is here:
https://sites.google.com/r-inla.org/inlabru/home

Finn
